prompt:
Build a resilient WebSocket client wrapper in src/. It takes a socket factory `(url) => { send(data), close(), onopen, onclose, onmessage, onerror }` (WebSocket-like; inject it so tests can use a fake) and a clock/timer abstraction you choose.
- connect() opens the socket. On unexpected close, reconnect with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, capped at 30s), resetting the backoff after a successful open.
- send(msg) sends immediately when open; while connecting/reconnecting it buffers messages (max 100, drop oldest) and flushes them in order on open.
- Heartbeat: send 'ping' every 15s while open; if no message arrives within 10s after a ping, treat the connection as dead and reconnect.
- close() closes permanently: no reconnects, buffered messages are discarded.
- Expose the current connection status and subscribe to status changes.

Implement the logic (no UI) for a 4-step checkout wizard in src/: shipping -> payment -> review -> confirmation.
- next() validates the current step's data and advances only if valid; back() goes to the previous step (not from confirmation).
- Each step has its own data and validation rules: shipping (name, address, postcode matching /^[0-9]{5}$/, country in US/CA/MX), payment (card number of 16 digits passing Luhn, expiry MM/YY not in the past given an injected 'today', cvc of 3 digits), review (accept terms must be true).
- Advancing from review calls an injected async submitOrder(data). While submitting, next/back are ignored. On success go to confirmation with the order id; on failure stay on review with the error message, allowing retry.
- Expose getState() for rendering: current step, per-field errors, whether next is allowed, submitting status, order id.

Implement a circuit breaker in src/ that wraps an async function.
- States: closed, open, half-open.
- Closed: calls pass through; after 5 consecutive failures, open.
- Open: calls fail fast with a CircuitOpenError without calling the function; after a 30s cooldown (use an injectable clock), the next call moves to half-open.
- Half-open: allow at most 1 trial call at a time (concurrent calls fail fast); if it succeeds, close and reset counts; if it fails, open again with the cooldown restarted.
- Calls exceeding a 5s timeout count as failures.
- Expose current state and an onStateChange callback.

Implement autosave logic for a document editor in src/ (no UI). It takes an injected async save(content) and timer functions.
- edit(content) marks the document as having unsaved changes and schedules a save 2s after the last edit (debounce).
- Only one save may be in flight. If edits happen during a save, another save of the latest content runs after the current one finishes.
- If a save fails, retry after 5s; edits made in the meantime reset that to the normal 2s debounce.
- flush() saves immediately (if there are unsaved changes) and returns a promise that resolves once everything is saved.
- Expose an indicator status for the UI: 'saved', 'unsaved', 'saving', or 'error' (with the error message), and a subscribe(listener) for changes.

Implement cart pricing in src/. Input: cart items {sku, category, unitPrice (cents), qty}, an optional coupon code, and the customer tier ('regular' | 'gold').
Rules:
- 10% off all items in the 'books' category.
- Buy 2 get 1 free on 'socks' (the cheapest units are free).
- Coupon SAVE5 gives $5 off orders whose subtotal (after item discounts) is at least $30; coupon FREESHIP waives shipping; an unknown coupon is an error.
- Gold tier gets an extra 5% off the subtotal (after item discounts, before coupons).
- Shipping is $7.99, free when the subtotal after all discounts is at least $50.
- Only one coupon per order.
Return a breakdown: line totals, each discount applied (with a human-readable label and amount), subtotal, shipping, total. All money in integer cents, with rounding to the nearest cent at each discount.

Implement authorization checks in src/ for a blogging platform: can(user, action, resource) -> boolean.
- Roles: admin, editor, author, viewer. Actions: read, create, update, delete, publish. Resources: post, comment, user.
- Admins can do everything.
- Editors can read/create/update/publish any post, and read/delete any comment; they cannot manage users.
- Authors can create posts, update and delete their own posts (only if unpublished), and read all published posts plus their own drafts; they can create comments and update/delete their own comments.
- Viewers can read published posts and comments, and create comments.
- Anyone can read and update their own user record; only admins can delete users.
- A suspended user (user.suspended === true) can only read.
Resources carry {type, ownerId, published?}. Users carry {id, role, suspended?}.

Implement a tiny HTTP router in src/ (no dependencies; do not use node:http in the router itself).
- router.add(method, pattern, handler), where a pattern like /users/:id/posts/:postId captures params and a trailing * matches the rest of the path.
- router.handle({method, path}) returns the handler's result, called with {params, query}; the query string is parsed from the path.
- When no route matches the path, return {status: 404}. When the path matches but not the method, return {status: 405, allow: [...methods]}.
- Static segments take priority over params (/users/me beats /users/:id) regardless of registration order.
- HEAD falls back to the GET handler when no HEAD route is registered.

Implement a small reactive spreadsheet-cell system in src/ (inspired by the Exercism 'react' exercise).
- createInput(value) gives a cell with get() and set(value).
- createComputed(deps, fn) gives a cell whose value is fn(...depValues), updated when dependencies change.
- Computed cells can have callbacks: addCallback(cb) returns a cancel function; a callback fires once per set() on an input, and only if that computed cell's value actually changed.
- Updates must be glitch-free: when an input changes, every computed cell sees a consistent set of dependency values (no intermediate states), and callbacks fire only after all cells have been updated.

Implement a media player controller (no UI) in src/. It wraps an injected media element with load(src), play() (returns a promise), pause(), seek(t), and emits events: 'canplay', 'waiting', 'playing', 'ended', 'error'.
- The player has a playlist: setPlaylist(tracks), next(), prev() (prev restarts the current track if more than 3s in), and select(index).
- Repeat modes: off, one, all. Shuffle: on/off (deterministic with an injected random function), with no repeats until every track has played.
- Show buffering while the element emits 'waiting' during playback.
- If a track errors, skip to the next track automatically; after 3 consecutive errors, stop with an error status.
- When the last track ends with repeat off, stop at the end.
- Expose getState() (status, current track, position, repeat, shuffle) and onChange.

Add a function isEnabled(flagName, user) in src/ that decides whether a feature flag is on for a user. Flags are loaded once from a plain JSON object like:
{ "newCheckout": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["u1"], "deny": ["u9"], "percent": 20 } }
- An unknown flag or enabled:false means off.
- deny wins over allow; allow wins over percent.
- percent rollout is deterministic per user and flag: hash flagName + user.id into a bucket 0-99 and enable if the bucket is below percent.
- Users without an id are only enabled at percent 100.

Implement a single-elevator controller simulation in src/ for a building with floors 0-9.
- request(floor) from the hall or the cab adds a stop.
- tick() advances time by one step: the elevator either moves one floor, opens its doors, keeps them open (doors stay open for 2 ticks), or closes them.
- It services stops in its current direction first (SCAN/elevator algorithm), then reverses; it goes idle when there are no stops.
- A request for the current floor while the doors are closing reopens them.
- An emergency_stop() halts it in place, ignoring requests until reset(), after which it resumes with its pending stops.
- Expose the current floor, direction, door state, and pending stops.

Implement a vending machine in src/.
- Products have slot codes (like 'A1'), prices in cents, and stock counts.
- insert(coin) accepts 5, 10, 25, 100 and 200 cent coins; others are returned immediately.
- select(code) dispenses the product if enough credit was inserted and it's in stock, and returns change using the fewest coins from the machine's coin inventory; if exact change can't be made, refuse the sale and keep the credit.
- Selecting with insufficient credit shows the price; selecting a sold-out product says sold out.
- cancel() refunds the inserted coins.
- Maintenance mode (entered with a service key) allows restocking and coin collection and rejects customer actions; leaving maintenance returns to normal.
- Every action returns a display message and any dispensed items/coins.

Implement an RFC 4180 CSV parser in src/ WITHOUT using the csv module.
- parse(text, delimiter=',') returns a list of rows (lists of strings).
- Support quoted fields containing delimiters, newlines, and escaped quotes (""), CRLF and LF line endings, empty fields, and a trailing newline at the end of input.
- Raise a ParseError with line and column for an unterminated quote, or a quote appearing in the middle of an unquoted field.
- Also provide parse_dicts(text) that uses the first row as headers, raising ParseError when a row has a different number of fields than the header.

Implement an e-commerce order lifecycle in src/.
- An order is created as pending_payment. Events: pay, ship(tracking_number), deliver, cancel, request_return, receive_return, refund(amount).
- Rules: you can only ship paid orders; cancel is allowed before shipping (a paid cancelled order is automatically marked as needing a full refund); a return can be requested within 30 days after delivery (injected clock); refunds can be partial, and the order is 'refunded' only when the total refunded equals the amount paid; refunding more than paid is an error.
- Invalid events raise InvalidTransition with the current state and the event.
- Each order keeps an audit log of (timestamp, event, from_state, to_state).

Implement a rate limiter in src/ for an API gateway.
- Token bucket per key: capacity N, refill rate R tokens per second, with an injectable clock.
- allow(key, cost=1) returns (allowed: bool, retry_after_seconds: float).
- Different plans have different limits: free = 10 capacity / 1 per second, pro = 100 / 20 per second; the key's plan is looked up via an injected function.
- Buckets for keys inactive for more than 10 minutes are evicted so memory doesn't grow without bound.

Implement application config loading in src/. The settings are: port (int, default 8080), host (str, default '127.0.0.1'), debug (bool, default False), database_url (str, required), workers (int, default 4, must be 1-64).
Sources, from lowest to highest precedence: defaults, a JSON file (path passed in, optional), environment variables prefixed APP_ (e.g. APP_PORT), then CLI-style overrides passed as a dict.
Convert types from the env strings (bool accepts true/false/1/0/yes/no), and raise a ConfigError listing ALL problems at once (missing required, bad types, out of range).
load_config(...) returns an immutable config object.

This repo already has src/notifications.py and tests. Add scheduled notifications: Notification can take an optional send_at timestamp; flush() must not send a notification before its send_at time (according to the notifier's clock). Also add cancel(notification), which prevents a pending or scheduled notification from ever being sent (cancelling an already-sent one is an error). pending() should include scheduled ones; add scheduled() that returns only the not-yet-due ones. Keep the existing tests passing.

Implement ten-pin bowling scoring in src/ (like the Exercism 'bowling' exercise).
- roll(pins) records a roll; score() returns the total once the game is complete.
- Handle strikes, spares, and the 10th frame's bonus rolls (up to 3 rolls in the 10th frame).
- Raise errors for invalid input: negative pins, more than 10 pins in a frame (respecting 10th-frame bonus rules), rolling after the game is over, and scoring an incomplete game.

Implement a simplified TCP connection state machine (RFC 793 states) as a Go package.
- States: CLOSED, LISTEN, SYN_SENT, SYN_RECEIVED, ESTABLISHED, FIN_WAIT_1, FIN_WAIT_2, CLOSING, TIME_WAIT, CLOSE_WAIT, LAST_ACK.
- Inputs are app calls (passive open, active open, close) and received segments (SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK, FIN, FIN+ACK, RST).
- Each input returns the segments to send (e.g. SYN+ACK) and the new state, or an error for an input that's invalid in the current state.
- RST from any synchronized state goes to CLOSED. TIME_WAIT goes to CLOSED after a Timeout() call (2MSL expiry).
- Provide a String() for states.

Implement a job scheduler as a Go package.
- A Scheduler with N workers runs submitted jobs (func(ctx context.Context) error).
- Submit returns a job ID; Status(id) returns queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled plus the attempt count and last error.
- Failed jobs are retried up to MaxRetries times with a fixed delay (configurable; tests should use short delays).
- Cancel(id) cancels a queued job (it never runs) or a running job (via its context; it ends as cancelled, not failed).
- Shutdown(ctx) stops accepting jobs, waits for running ones to finish, and marks still-queued jobs as cancelled.
- Must be race-free under `go test -race`.

Implement a command-line argument parser as a Go package (do not use the flag package).
- Define commands with subcommands (e.g. `tool remote add <name> <url>`), each with its own flags.
- Flags: long (--verbose), short (-v), bundled short booleans (-abc), values as --name=value, --name value, or -n value; repeated flags collect into a list where declared as such.
- Positional args are validated by count (exact, or at-least/at-most N).
- `--` ends flag parsing.
- Generate help text listing a command's subcommands, flags and usage; -h/--help returns it.
- Return clear errors: unknown flag, missing value, unknown subcommand, wrong number of args.

Implement a lexer (tokenizer) as a Go package for a small expression language:
- Integers and decimals (1, 3.14, but '1.' is an error), identifiers (letters, digits, underscore; not starting with a digit), keywords (let, if, else, fn, return, true, false), string literals in double quotes with escapes \n \t \" \\, operators (+ - * / % == != < <= > >= = && || ! ( ) { } , ;), line comments // to end of line, and block comments /* */ (not nested).
- Each token carries its kind, literal text, and line:column.
- Errors (unterminated string or block comment, bad escape, unexpected character) carry a position, and the lexer continues after reporting them, collecting all errors.
- Tokenize(src) returns tokens (ending with EOF) and errors.

Implement a controller for a two-road traffic intersection (north-south and east-west) as a Go package, driven by Tick(seconds) calls and input events.
- Normal cycle: NS green 30s -> NS yellow 4s -> all red 2s -> EW green 30s -> EW yellow 4s -> all red 2s -> repeat.
- Pedestrian button for a road: if that road's light is red, shorten the current green phase of the other road to at most 10s remaining (once per cycle); the walk signal is on during the pedestrian's road's green.
- Emergency vehicle approaching from a road: go to yellow (if a different road is green), then all red, then green for the emergency road, held until EmergencyCleared(), then resume the normal cycle.
- Night mode (on/off): both roads flash yellow; leaving night mode starts at all red then NS green.
- Expose the current light for each road and the walk signals.

Implement a parking garage system as a Rust library.
- The garage has a capacity. enter(plate, now) issues a ticket if there's space (otherwise Full).
- pay(ticket, now): fee is $3/hour, rounded up per started hour, max $20/day, first 15 minutes free. After paying, the driver has 15 minutes to exit; otherwise they owe the difference for the extra time.
- exit(ticket, now) opens the gate only if paid and within the grace period.
- lost_ticket(plate, now) charges the daily max for each started day and allows exit.
- A ticket can't be used twice. Expose occupancy.
- Time is passed in explicitly (e.g. as seconds), not read from the system.

Implement an inline Markdown-to-HTML converter as a Rust library (no crates). - Support **bold**, *italic* and _italic_, `code` (contents not parsed further and HTML-escaped), [links](url), and backslash escapes (\*, \_, \`, \[, \\). - Nesting like **bold *italic* bold** works; unmatched markers are output literally. - HTML special characters in text are escaped (&, <, >, "). - Only inline content: one paragraph string in, an HTML fragment string out (no

wrapper).

Implement a text buffer with undo/redo as a Rust library.
- Operations: insert(pos, text), delete(range), and replace(range, text), with positions in chars (not bytes; must handle multi-byte UTF-8).
- undo() and redo() step through history; a new edit after undo clears the redo history.
- Consecutive single-character inserts at adjacent positions (typing) are grouped into one undo step, but a group breaks on whitespace, after 1 second of inactivity (timestamps passed in), or on cursor jumps.
- The history is limited to 100 undo steps.
- Expose text(), can_undo(), can_redo().

Implement a package dependency resolver as a Rust library.
- Input: a registry of packages, each with multiple versions (semver x.y.z), each version declaring dependencies with constraints: exact (=1.2.3), caret (^1.2.0 means >=1.2.0 and <2.0.0), or tilde (~1.2.0 means >=1.2.0 and <1.3.0).
- resolve(root_deps) picks one version per package that satisfies all constraints, preferring the highest versions, and backtracks when needed.
- Return an install order where dependencies come before dependents.
- Errors: unknown package, no satisfying version (report which constraints conflicted), dependency cycle (report the cycle path).

Implement a byte-stream frame decoder and encoder in C for a SLIP-like serial protocol, as used in an embedded UART receive path.
- Frames are delimited by END (0xC0). Inside a frame, ESC (0xDB) followed by ESC_END (0xDC) means 0xC0, and ESC followed by ESC_ESC (0xDD) means 0xDB; ESC followed by anything else is a protocol error and drops the frame.
- The last byte of each decoded frame is a checksum: the XOR of all preceding payload bytes; a mismatch drops the frame.
- The decoder is fed one byte at a time (decoder_feed(dec, byte)) from an interrupt handler: no malloc, a fixed 256-byte max payload (oversized frames are dropped), and a callback invoked with each valid frame.
- Consecutive END bytes (empty frames) are ignored.
- Count dropped frames by reason (bad escape, bad checksum, overflow).
- Provide an encoder that writes a framed and escaped buffer from a payload.

Implement a smart thermostat controller in Zig.
- Modes set by the user: off, heat, cool, auto. Setpoint in tenths of a degree Celsius.
- update(temperature, now_seconds) is called periodically and returns the equipment command: idle, heating, cooling (plus whether the fan is on).
- Hysteresis: in heat mode, start heating below setpoint - 0.5C and stop at setpoint + 0.5C; cooling is the mirror image. Auto mode heats or cools as needed, with a 2C deadband around the setpoint.
- Compressor protection: after cooling stops, cooling may not restart for 5 minutes.
- The fan runs while heating or cooling, and for 60s after either stops (fan overrun).
- Fan setting: auto (as above) or on (always on).
- Changing the mode while heating or cooling stops the equipment immediately (the overrun and compressor rules still apply).
